_readme: Optional per-unit absolute-time calibration. Each key under 'boards' is one physical board's factory-burned unique ID, exactly as reported in this project's serial handshake (visible in the console as '[INFO] board_program=... chip_id=...' when a board connects, or in a .dat file's header). 'ppm_offset' is how many parts-per-million the device's reported elapsed time exceeds true elapsed time, as measured by comparing the device's own reported duration against an independent time reference (e.g. an NTP-synchronized PC clock, over a long recording -- see README.md). Positive means the device's clock runs fast. plot.py applies corrected_time = raw_time / (1 + ppm_offset / 1e6) to any recording from a board listed here; boards with no entry are left uncorrected (this is the default -- calibration is opt-in, per unit, and this file starts empty). This is a per-unit measurement, not a general claim about the board type -- see README.md's timing-precision discussion for why.
